newsitem.title: UK: Shell faces investor vote on ethics - paper.
newsitem.headline: Shell faces investor vote on ethics - paper.

text.p: Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc, the UK arm of the Anglo-Dutch oil giant, is set to face a call from institutional shareholders to improve its accountability on green and human rights issues at its annual general meeting in May, said the Financial Times on Monday.
The report said investors holding just under one percent of shares will call for new Shell procedures to be set up governing environmental and human rights issues.
Pirc, the corporate governance group advising the shareholders concerned, claimed it would be the first resolution of its kind in the UK.

The investor group includes pension funds, religious groups and an academic fund who claim that Shell's reputation was sullied by rows over the aborted plans to dispose of the Brent Spar oil rig at sea and criticisms of its human rights and environmental record in Nigeria.
Green groups have claimed that Shell polluted the Niger Delta region and allegedly helped the Nigerian government persecute the region's Ogoni tribe -- allegations which Shell has denied.
